standard.title: Reflect on influences to inform practice
standard.description: reflect on the ways that they and other artists respond to influences to inform choices they make in their own visual arts practice
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use teacher feedback to reflect on their practice (AC9AVA6D02). They have not yet investigated how other artists respond to influences and used that investigation to articulate and inform their own practice choices.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students reflect on how they and other artists respond to influences — materials, emotions, cultural context, other artworks — to make informed and documented choices in own visual arts practice.

nodes.label: Identifying influences on artistic choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the influences on an artist's choices — including material properties, emotional responses, cultural context and investigation of other artists — and explain how these shape the work
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two influences on an artist's choices in a given work; explain how each influence shaped a specific decision in the work
nodes.typical_width: Investigate a range of influences on an artist's practice (material, emotional, cultural, contextual); explain how these converge in specific works and choices
wider: Investigate how an artist responds to sensory qualities of materials as a generative influence — analyse how material properties direct the work's development
Compare how two artists from different cultural contexts respond to similar influences — analyse what differs and why
Investigate how an artist's emotional or personal experience becomes a generative influence rather than just a theme — analyse how this shapes visual convention choices

response_modes.reason: Students need to build a repertoire of influence types — material properties, emotional experience, cultural context, investigation of other artists, sensory stimuli — before they can meaningfully reflect on which influences are shaping their own practice. A single influence type gives too narrow a lens for genuine reflection.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two influence types on an artist's choices
Explains how each influence shaped a specific decision — not just lists influences
Does not reduce 'influence' to 'inspiration' without explanation

nodes.label: Reflecting on own influences and practice choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on the influences on their own practice choices and document how those influences are shaping specific decisions
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one influence on a specific choice in own practice; explain the connection between the influence and the decision made
nodes.typical_width: Use teacher and student set goals to reflect on and practise skills over time; document how specific influences (investigation of other artists, material properties, personal experience) are shaping practice choices; evaluate outcomes
wider: Develop an extended reflection documenting how multiple influences converge and sometimes conflict in own practice decisions
Explore colour theory in depth (harmonious/contrasting palettes, emotional associations, cultural meanings) and apply systematically — document the reasoning at each compositional decision
Investigate sustainable material practices and reflect on how sustainability constraints become productive influences rather than limitations

response_modes.reason: Sustained reflective practice — setting goals, practising, evaluating against criteria, adjusting — requires disciplined iteration rather than broader contexts. The skill is in the reflection cycle itself: students who practise the cycle repeatedly develop genuine self-awareness as artists. More influence types don't help; more rounds of the reflection cycle do.

Students commonly describe what they did without reasoning through why they made specific choices or how influences shaped them. Scaffolding the reasoning (what influenced this decision, how did I respond to it, what alternative did I reject and why?) builds the reflective vocabulary that makes documentation meaningful rather than descriptive.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one specific influence on a practice decision
Explains the connection between influence and decision — not just 'I decided to...'
Documentation uses visual arts terminology and goes beyond surface description

nodes.label: Using reflection to develop visual arts practice over time
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use reflection on influences — their own and other artists' — as a sustained practice that develops over time and produces increasingly informed and distinctive artistic choices
nodes.minimum_width: Show at least one example where reflection on an influence led to a changed practice direction; document the before/after and explain what changed and why
nodes.typical_width: Document how practice has developed over a unit as a result of sustained reflection on influences; show how reflection has produced increasingly informed and distinctive choices
wider: Build on understanding of composition to explore multiple approaches to representing space and depth — document how each investigation changes subsequent compositional decisions
Develop a personal artistic statement that articulates the influences currently shaping own practice and how those influences are being engaged and adapted
Reflect on the work of multiple artists alongside own explorations — document convergences and divergences and explain what they reveal about own developing practice identity

response_modes.reason: This node integrates influence identification (Node 1), reflective practice cycles (Node 2), and evidence of development over time into a coherent account of own practice development. Students who can reflect on single influences but cannot demonstrate sustained development over a unit have not met the descriptor's demand for reflection that informs practice.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The personal artistic statement direction gives advancing students a genuine opportunity to synthesise their reflection into a articulated practice identity — this is rich beyond the minimum because it requires students to think about themselves as developing artists with a perspective, not just as students completing tasks.
success_criteria: Shows at least one example where reflection led to a changed practice direction
Documentation demonstrates development over time — not a single reflection moment
Reflection on influences is connected to increasingly distinctive and informed choices
